steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Cook egg noodles according to package directions.

While noodles are cooking, brown the ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium high heat. Reduce heat to low, add the tomato sauce, stir well, and let simmer for 1 minute. Add the cream cheese and cottage cheese, stirring together until well blended. Then stir in the egg noodles and sour cream until all ingredients are well mixed. Pour into a 2 quart casserole dish.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 30 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

raw_recipe.headline: Double Cheese Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This is similar to lasagna. It's fairly easy to prepare, and my picky eaters love it! The cheeses are cream cheese and cottage cheese, which enables you to control the fat content without cutting on flavor. Garnish with some grated Parmesan cheese, if desired.

review.reviewBody: Well, with A LOT of doctoring, this recipe turned out great! First, I made a much yummier sauce then this recipe called for. I used Sun Dried Tomatoe sauce, and garlic tomatoe paste, a little brown sugar, some hot sauce, lots of garlic, ect. I didn't mix all the cheeses/sour cream in to the meat mixture because that sounded a little yucky to me. Instead I assembled it like you would lasagna, with a layer of the cheese mixture all on it's own. So, for that I didn't actually measure the cheeses or sour cream. Just threw what I thought would be good in a bowl and stired it up. I also added half each of a yellow and red pepper, and about 1 cup of grated aged cheddar cheese. I then, in a greased casserole dish, put half the noodles, all the cheese mixture, half the meat sauce, remaining noodles, remaining meat suuce, and finally topped it all off with some more grated cheddar and a sprinkle of parm. Yumm!!! Loved this, at least the way I made it. It's a great idea, just play with it to make it the likes of your family. Thanx for this great idea though! :)

Simple and quick dinner to prepare. I divided this casserole into three small dishes. One to be eaten and the other two to freeze. Because the sour cream, cottage cheese and cream cheese are mixed with other ingredients it froze well and baked up beautifully. I baked the frozen one in the toaster oven for 1 hour at 350°. This would also be very good made with sausage rather than hamburger. This recipe has been "faceless" since at least September 2000. Glad to finally add a picture.

I made this for the first time ever tonight. It was really great! My husband and I loved it! Very minor changes-didn't have enough egg noodles so added about a cup of farfalle pasta to the mix. Also, added about a half tsp. each of oregano and basil to the meat mixture. Had a half green pepper so added that in with the onion. And, sprinkled top of casserole with some sharp cheddar cheese. It was so good and I will make this again, for sure!

Great recipe I remember my mom making years ago. I changed a few thing to make it more like I remembered, but nice to have the portions! Changes I made were spaghetti sauce vs just tomato sauce and I layered 1/2 the noodle mixture on the bottom, topped with 1/2the sauce, the more noodles, more sauce. I baked in a 9x 13 pan. Tonight I am going to try and cut the recipe in 1/2, last time I had to share it with my neighbor and their kids, way too much for 2. But yummy comfort food for sure!
Loved it! I used ground turkey, light sour cream, neufeuchtal cheese, and low fat cottage cheese. So good!

My 14 yr old daughter found this recipe on here and made it for us for dinner a few nights ago... we took the advice of other reviews and used salsa sauce instead of tomato sauce and added 1 cup shredded cheese in mix and on top! Very filling meal, even the picky younger two ate this! Will make this one again!

This was a good recipe. I changed some things that other members had suggested. I used crushed tomatoes with garlic and basil. I also skipped the cottage cheese because my husband doesn't like it and substitued with mozzarella and parmesan shredded cheeses,reserving some to place on top of the cassarole. I also used onion powder, about 1 Tbsp, since I didn't have any onions on hand. I didn't add salt when I was cooking because I wasn't sure how salty the cheeses would make the cassarole, but it definately needed it.

Too easy to taste this good! I can have this dish on the table in about 45 minutes. It is also great using diced chicken. If you like italian based dishes and are time poor, you have to try this recipe. I do add 1/2 teaspoon of basil and oregano for a more italian taste and top with grated cheese before baking and substitue tomato sauce for tomato soup. Serve with garden salad, ranch dressing and garlic bread - excellent!!!!

Rave reviews from my family! I first made this exactly how the recipe reads and it turned out well, however, we do lots of leftovers for lunches and the noodles were really mushy the next day. The second time I made it I subbed the noodles for steamed shredded cabbage…it was a big hit again.

I added a few spices to the sauce (onion powder, garlic powder, italian seasoning, fresh ground pepper) but other than that, I kept to the recipe. The little kids liked it okay, my husband and I weren't real big fans. I think this would have been better had it included some shredded cheese and cut back on the sour cream a touch.

I am mother to the two most picky eaters and they loved this dish!!! I made only minor adjustments. I pre-seasoned the beef with pepper, lowery's seasoning salt, and garlic powder. Then before popping it in the oven I added 2c. mozzarella cheese 1c. stirred in 1c. on top.
I’ve been making the recipe since 1971 when I received my Betty Crocker Recipe cards in the mail. Everyone has always loved it.
It's a good recipe, and although it doesn't LOOK too appetizing, it tastes pretty good.
a keeper.....the entire family loved this....we made this with left over meat we had and it worked out nice to help clear the refrig of leftovers....thanks for the great recipe
A little bland. Even without much flavor my family didn't finish theirs. I won't make again.
This was like a lazy lasagna. We enjoyed it and it was good reheated.
My kids love it when they see that this is for dinner. My husband and I like a little more flavor in our food. But it's a very accessible dish.
Very yummy. My whole family loved it from my four year old to my husband. I did need to add spices, and I added chedder cheese on top.

It is nice and creamy. My husband and son Love this recipe. I made it and the next day it was gone!!!

 Reviewed by: H. Chandler

My husband who does not like cottage cheese loved it. He even asked me to make it again. Then I told him what all the ingredients were. Next time I'm going to ues more of the cheeses. OH I uesed ground trukey, fat free everything.. next time I will ues real cream cheese.
